overview: The Medford School Committee is the governing body responsible for the fiscal oversight, infrastructure planning, and educational policy of the Medford Public Schools. Spanning terms from 2022 to 2026, the committee manages the district's participation in the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) process for major facility reconstruction and sets annual operating budgets. Its work includes evaluating district leadership, approving labor contracts, and responding to shifting enrollment patterns through redistricting and space utilization studies. As of late 2026, the committee is finalizing schematic designs for elementary school repairs and implementing a significant expansion of district-wide after-school programming.

threads.name: Medford High School Building Project
threads.summary: Following acceptance into the MSBA core program in late 2023, the committee established the Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee to oversee a multi-year reconstruction project. The body appointed Left Field as the Owner's Project Manager and developed a comprehensive educational plan to guide the facility's design and vocational program expansions. In 2026, the project faced challenges regarding a 1967 DCR deed restriction on Edgley Field, prompting the committee to eliminate several design alternatives and adopt modified plans to avoid restricted land. The committee continues to refine the project's schematic design and sustainability goals while coordinating with the MSBA on reimbursement rates.

threads.name: Budget and Financial Oversight
threads.summary: The committee navigated a preliminary $2.5 million deficit in fiscal year 2024 caused by structural underbudgeting in transportation and legal costs. To stabilize district finances, the committee advocated for local tax override questions, which voters approved in late 2024 to fund the restoration of teaching, nursing, and literacy positions. Subsequent budget cycles focused on closing gaps for level services, with the committee approving a $77.75 million operating budget for FY25 and finalizing the FY27 budget by adjusting administrative costs and utilizing revolving funds. Recent financial reporting in late 2026 shows a focus on managing risks associated with special education transportation and facility energy costs.

threads.name: Elementary School Capacity and Facility Repairs
threads.summary: Severe overcrowding at the Roberts Elementary School prompted the committee to explore short-term space solutions, including the relocation of preschool classrooms to other buildings and the hiring of additional staff. Concurrently, the committee addressed failing infrastructure at multiple schools, authorizing over $25 million in bonds for HVAC replacements at the McGlynn and Andrews schools. For broader district maintenance, the body submitted Accelerated Repair applications to the MSBA for the Roberts, Missituk, and Brooks schools to address roof and heating system failures. In late 2026, the committee selected a geothermal heat pump system for the Missituck project and approved a schematic design for electrification at Roberts.

threads.name: District Leadership and Superintendent Search
threads.summary: The committee managed the transition from Superintendent Marice Edouard-Vincent, who departed in early 2025 after seven years of service, to new leadership. Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi was first appointed as Interim Superintendent to ensure continuity during active facility projects and budget cycles. After conducting an evaluation of her first year and soliciting community feedback on leadership priorities, the committee voted in February 2026 to appoint Galusi as the permanent superintendent. The committee subsequently approved a three-year contract for Galusi and realigned the evaluation schedule to match the academic year.

threads.name: After-School Program Expansion
threads.summary: Long-standing capacity issues and waitlists for before- and after-school care led the committee to partner with the BASIC collaborative for a comprehensive program assessment. Based on these recommendations, the committee approved a restructuring that transitioned programs to a model featuring full-time site directors and specialized curriculum leaders to increase seat capacity by 150. To fund this expansion, the committee adopted a new tuition rate card with tiered fee structures and multi-day flexibility for families. By October 2026, the district reported a 50 percent increase in enrollment and a 68 percent reduction in waitlist numbers.

threads.name: Student Advisory and Engagement
threads.summary: The committee established a formal partnership with a student-led advisory council to incorporate student voices into policy decisions regarding school rules and culture. Early discussions focused on student-proposed reforms to homework time limits, the backpack ban, and school bus safety at high-traffic loading zones. The committee eventually formalized student representation by designating a recurring agenda block for council presentations and establishing a rotation for members to attend student meetings. Students have since used this platform to advocate for late bus services and present research on increasing representation in advanced coursework.

threads.name: Curriculum, Policy, and Accountability
threads.summary: The committee regularly reviews district-wide performance data, including MCAS and NWEA MAP assessments, to inform targeted instructional interventions. In response to state ballot initiatives, the body updated graduation requirements to replace the MCAS competency mandate with successful completion of aligned coursework. The committee also modernized its policy manual by adopting regulations for the ethical use of generative artificial intelligence and updating Title IX grievance procedures to comply with federal standards. Recent efforts include developing a new district strategic plan to align curriculum across grade levels and improve early literacy benchmarks.

periods.narrative: This term was defined by a successful funding override, a leadership transition to an interim superintendent, and the selection of an Owner's Project Manager for the high school project.
The committee appointed a permanent superintendent, addressed deed restrictions at the high school site, and finalized major bond authorizations for elementary school HVAC and roof repairs.
